html:
The Washoe, Wašišiw in their own language, are a Native American people of Lake Tahoe and the valleys of the eastern Sierra Nevada, on the border of California and Nevada. Their language is unlike those of their neighbours, the Northern Paiute and Miwok.

Lake Tahoe was the heart of their world. In summer they fished and gathered at the lake; in autumn they went to the pine nut groves of the Pine Nut Mountains; in winter they lived in the valleys below. Washoe women were famous basket makers, and the weaver Dat So La Lee won fame in the early 1900s.

The silver strikes of the Comstock Lode from 1859 brought miners who cut down the pine forests and fenced the valleys, leaving the Washoe with only small scattered colonies.
